studies.Reference: Cabbage and Sauerkraut Consumption in Adolescence and Adulthood and Breast Cancer Risk among US-Resident Polish Migrant Women.
studies.Authors: Pathak DR, Stein AD, He JP, Noel MM, Hembroff L, Nelson DA, Vigneau F, Shen T, Scott LJ, Charzewska J, Wajszczyk B, Clark K, Rybaczyk LA, Pathak BA, Błaszczyk D, Bankowski A, Willett WC
studies.Journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
studies.comparison_type: High adolescent and adult consumption vs Low adolescent and adult consumption
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Food frequency questionnaires assessed diet during adulthood and age 12-13 years.

extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Greater consumption of total and raw/short-cooked cabbage/sauerkraut foods either during adolescence or adulthood was associated with significantly reduced BC risk.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: Cases were 20-79 years old with histological/cytological confirmation of invasive BC.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Consumption of total, raw/short-cooked, and long-cooked cabbage/sauerkraut foods was categorized as low, medium, or high (frequency of servings/week).
